notes: Live Atlassian MCP fetch is non-deterministic in eval subagents, so each prompt supplies the ticket as a file (treated as already-fetched) plus a small fixture codebase to verify claims against. Evals 1-3 leave the approval gate intact, so autonomous runs stop at phase 5 (present-for-approval) without editing — phases 2-4 (intent, claim verification, plan reconciliation) are the differentiated value being graded there. Evals 4 and 5 are the exceptions: both pre-grant approval in the prompt so the run proceeds into phase 6 (implement) and works against a copy of the fixture, to exercise and grade the discipline the other evals never reach — eval 4 the red/green TDD loop, eval 5 the phase 7 coverage sweep. Eval 5's fixture is built so that TDD alone leaves a gap: the ticket asks only for percentage discount codes, but making a redeemed code actually reduce what the customer pays also requires changing formatReceipt, which the ticket never mentions and which pricing.test.js never imports. A run that stops at a green suite ships that gap; only the sweep catches it. Because the run works on a copy outside any git repo, eval 5 also exercises the sweep's non-git fallback (inventory from its own edit record) and the mutation check that substitutes for the unavailable natural RED.
